items.readable_text:
Content:
There are two ways to add a positive number to a negative number. Let's work out the value of [MATH: -5+7] using both methods.

Content:
Method 1 - Picturing a Number Line

Content:
When we add, we move to the right on the number line.

Content:
So, to add [MATH: 7] to [MATH: -5,] we start at [MATH: -5] on a number line and move [MATH: 7] spaces to the right.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/2b4639aa8389cbd95c5bde180ee50bea]

Content:
When we do this, we land at [MATH: 2.] Therefore, [MATH: -5+7 =2.]

Content:
Method 2 - Subtraction in Reverse

Content:
Adding a positive number to a negative number is like subtraction in reverse. To turn the addition into a subtraction, we must switch the numbers around.

Content:
So, to work out [MATH: {\color{red}{-5}} + {\color{blue}{7}},] we can switch the numbers around to get
[MATH: \,{\color{blue}{7}} {\color{red}{\,-\,5}} =2.]

Content:
We're allowed to swap the numbers because addition is commutative, which means the order in which we add two numbers does not matter.

items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose that we want to calculate [MATH: -\dfrac 1 3 + \dfrac 5 3.]

Content:
Since both fractions have a common denominator of [MATH: 3,] we can combine them to form one fraction:

Content:
[MATH: -\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{5}{3} =\dfrac{-1+5}{3}]

Content:
To compute the numerator, we can use either method that we've learned.

Content:
Method 1 - Picturing a Number Line

Content:
To add [MATH: 5] to [MATH: -1,] we start at [MATH: -1] on a number line and move [MATH: 5] spaces to the right.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/9ec0a03a326bcb211b5101a5421201c6]

Content:
We end up at [MATH: 4.] So [MATH: -1+5=4,] and therefore
[MATH: \dfrac{-1+5}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}.]

Content:
Method 2 - Subtraction in Reverse

Content:
We can swap the order of the numbers in the numerator and then compute the resulting subtraction:
[MATH: (− 1 + 5)/(3) = (5 − 1)/(3) = (4)/(3)]

Content:
So, we conclude that [MATH: -\dfrac1 3 + \dfrac 5 3 = \dfrac{4}{3}.]

Content:
Note: If two fractions have different denominators, we need to put them over a common denominator first and then subtract!

sections.normalized_html:
We put both fractions over a common denominator of [MATH: 6] and then add the numerators. This gives [MATH: -\dfrac{7}{6} + \dfrac{5}{3} = -\dfrac{7}{6} + \dfrac{10}{6} = \dfrac{-7+10}{6}.]

To compute the numerator, we can use either Method 1 or Method 2, shown below.

Method 1 - Picturing a Number Line

To add [MATH: 10] to [MATH: -7,] we start at [MATH: -7] on a number line and move [MATH: 10] spaces to the right.

So, [MATH: -7 + 10 = 3.] Therefore, [MATH: \dfrac{-7 + 10}{6} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}.]

Method 2 - Subtraction in Reverse

We can swap the order of the numbers in the numerator, and we get [MATH: \dfrac{-7 + 10}{6} = \dfrac{10 - 7}{6} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}.]

So, we conclude that [MATH: -\dfrac{7}{6} + \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}.]

Item 9 — Tutorial: Adding a Positive Fraction to a Negative Fraction

Content:
Suppose that we want to calculate [MATH: -\dfrac 1 3 + \dfrac 5 3.]

Content:
Since both fractions have a common denominator of [MATH: 3,] we can combine them to form one fraction:

Content:
[MATH: -\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{5}{3} =\dfrac{-1+5}{3}]

Content:
To compute the numerator, we can use either method that we've learned.

Content:
Method 1 - Picturing a Number Line

Content:
To add [MATH: 5] to [MATH: -1,] we start at [MATH: -1] on a number line and move [MATH: 5] spaces to the right.

We end up at [MATH: 4.] So [MATH: -1+5=4,] and therefore
[MATH: \dfrac{-1+5}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}.]

Content:
Method 2 - Subtraction in Reverse

Content:
We can swap the order of the numbers in the numerator and then compute the resulting subtraction:
[MATH: (− 1 + 5)/(3) = (5 − 1)/(3) = (4)/(3)]

So, we conclude that [MATH: -\dfrac1 3 + \dfrac 5 3 = \dfrac{4}{3}.]

To compute the numerator, we can use either Method 1 or Method 2, shown below.

[MATH: \dfrac{-7 + 10}{6} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}.]

Method 2 - Subtraction in Reverse

We can swap the order of the numbers in the numerator, and we get
[MATH: \dfrac{-7 + 10}{6} = \dfrac{10 - 7}{6} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}.]

So, we conclude that [MATH: -\dfrac{7}{6} + \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}.]
